caption:
This morning’s post was about Anthropic rebuilding version control because agent-written code pushed git into the bottleneck.

200× smaller infrastructure footprint versus its previous git mirroring setup.
25% CPU capacity win in CI, with checkouts moving from minutes to seconds.
A Google publication is cited for 60–70k commits per workday in Piper, but this point was not confirmed on the cited source at check time.

My take: the lesson is still workflow first. Simple review, rollback, and operational control beat complexity that only looks impressive.

Comment CHECK and I will DM you what I find.

Sources in the first comment.

scenes: This morning, the post said Anthropic rebuilt version control because agent-written code pushed git into the main bottleneck. I went back in to check the surrounding numbers.
First, Anthropic says Scion made the infrastructure much lighter, with a 200-times smaller footprint than its previous git mirroring setup.
Second, the operational gain was not just faster checkouts. Anthropic says CI alone saw a 25 percent CPU capacity win.
Third, a Google publication is cited for 60 to 70 thousand commits per workday, but we could not confirm that on the cited page.
My take: workflow still matters more than tooling here. If you use Piper or similar systems, Comment CHECK and tell me.
